scenes.title: 앞 편의 회전값에서 중간 자세로
lines: The previous episode found the rotation difference from the starting to the target orientation. We now construct intermediate orientations along that rotation.

scenes.title: 두 끝점만으로는 중간 화면이 비어 있습니다
lines: After observing the body changing direction, can we make intermediate poses by mixing the four numbers at the start and end?

scenes.title: 티는 회전 차이 중 얼마나 적용할지입니다
lines: In delta to the power t, t is the exponent on delta; the expression does not square t.
With a z ninety-degree delta and t equal to one half, apply half the difference, forty-five degrees, to the starting orientation.
We will now calculate weights that keep the intermediate orientation on the unit arc.

scenes.title: 절반 자세는 움직임 중간에 있습니다
lines: Observe connected poses in Skate 3. Red follows the body direction.
Blue follows the visible board length. Follow takeoff, the airborne pose and landing separately.
The fraction for constructing intermediate poses is t. The previous forty-five degrees was a worked example, not an angle measured here.

scenes.title: 내적과 아크코사인이 호의 각도를 찾는 이유
lines: Following an arc requires the angle between its endpoints. Begin with the familiar unit circle in a plane.
The rightward unit vector is one, zero. A thirty-degree vector is square root three over two, one half. Multiplying corresponding entries and adding gives square root three over two.
That number is cosine of thirty degrees. Arccosine performs the reverse lookup and returns thirty degrees.
For quaternions, the dot sums four component products and gives the angle alpha in the section joining the two unit points. Alpha must be distinguished from the object's physical rotation.

scenes.title: 움직이는 몸체와 단위 방향의 길이
lines: Red follows the body; blue follows the board direction.
Their directions change in the air before another landing.
Unit length in the calculation is a condition on the stored direction values.
It does not set the game travel distance or the displayed line length to one.

scenes.title: 맞는 식에도 입력 검사가 필요한 이유
lines: We found the unit arc, but its denominator becomes small as the endpoints coincide. Handle nearly identical orientations first.

scenes.title: 관찰한 중간 자세를 작은 계산으로
lines: To verify the observation made with a moving camera, fix the camera and z axis and compute the intermediate poses of a ninety-degree turn.

scenes.title: 방향의 변화와 지나가는 속도 나누기
lines: Watch the order in which the red body line and blue board line change.
Travel distance and the fraction between orientations are different values. The camera also follows the action.
Fast-looking screen motion does not establish constant angular speed. We will state the timing conditions separately in the calculation.

scenes.title: 자세의 비율과 실제 시간을 연결하기
lines: Using intermediate orientations in playback also requires deciding how t increases over time.

scenes.title: 한 바퀴의 기록이 끝 자세에 남을까요
lines: Even after choosing a timing rule, we must check whether the final orientation retains the record of an extra complete turn.

scenes.title: 지나온 회전의 기록과 현재 자세 나누기
lines: The red body direction changes and becomes upright again.
The current pose and the rotation history are different information.
This is a different excerpt. Follow the blue board direction separately as well.
Passing the final orientation does not also store how many turns occurred.

scenes.title: 중간 자세를 다음 작업에 넘기려면
lines: We now have an intermediate orientation at one instant. Editing its angles and applying it to many vertices call for different representations.
Keep the same body axes while passing that orientation between editable angles, interpolation quaternions and matrices that transform vectors.

scenes.title: 보간한 자세를 다음 계산에 넘기기
lines: Between two orientations, we chose a path, kept unit length and specified how t follows physical time. Extra turn history needed separate storage.
We now pass one intermediate orientation to the next task. The next episode retains the same object and axes while converting angles, quaternions and matrices and verifying the same rotation.

scenes.title: 다른 숫자가 같은 자세인지 확인하기
lines: The first episode found intermediate orientations and chose representations for different tasks. We now convert the same pose between angles, quaternions and matrices.
First declare axes and multiplication order, then use a small direction vector and round trips to verify that the rotation remains the same.

scenes.title: 보이는 방향에서 각도 읽기로 이어가기
lines: Observe the same body lean and become upright. Red follows the body; blue follows the board.
Turning a direction into numbers first requires axes. These screen lines are projected observations through the camera.
The next triangle is a worked example with fixed axes. Read its length and direction angle from its horizontal and vertical components.

scenes.title: 에이탄 투와 하이폿을 작은 수로 읽기
lines: Before extracting angles from a matrix, consider two functions. Hypot returns a right triangle's hypotenuse: horizontal three and vertical four give the square root of their squared sum, five.
Atan2 takes vertical and horizontal values together to recover a direction angle. One and one give forty-five degrees, while their signs identify the quadrant.
These tools read directions, but singular orientations merge information. Recovering one unique original angle set then requires a separate convention.

scenes.title: 같은 세 축을 쿼터니언에서 읽기
lines: Now build the three axes from the quaternion as well as the angles, and compare the resulting direction vector.

scenes.title: 몸체와 보드에는 다른 방향이 붙어 있습니다
lines: Red follows the body. Blue follows the visible board length.
Their directions change separately and then reconnect.
Distinguish the objects before comparing calculated results for the same direction vector.

scenes.title: 한 자세를 여러 작업에 넘겨 쓰기
lines: Compare the red body line and blue board line.
The moving object has one orientation at a particular instant.
That pose can be expressed as angles for editing, a quaternion for interpolation or a matrix for applying it to vectors.
The next round trip checks whether the converted numbers produce the same direction.

scenes.title: 행렬에서 회전값을 읽을 때 나눗셈을 지키기
lines: After converting a quaternion to a matrix, check the reverse path. Trace is simply the sum of the three entries on the main diagonal.
For a z one-hundred-eighty-degree matrix, minus one plus minus one plus one gives minus one. The quaternion's w is zero, so a method that divides by w cannot be used throughout.
The next calculation chooses a sufficiently large component to divide by, then checks that it rebuilds the same matrix.

scenes.title: 같은 자세를 바꿔 적는 것과 실제로 돌리는 것
lines: Follow the red body direction. Even with a following camera, the body has one orientation at each instant.
Converting a matrix to a quaternion does not add another physical rotation.
This is a different excerpt. The blue board direction changes before another landing.
Separate an action that changes the pose from a conversion that writes the same pose in different numbers.

scenes.title: 카메라의 그림과 몸체의 자세 구분하기
lines: Follow the red body line while the camera also moves with it.
The tilt projected on screen is not the body three-dimensional angle.
Continue observing the same object in a different excerpt.
Verifying recovered angles requires declared axes and rotation data in addition to the camera observation.

scenes.title: 축과 각도를 되찾을 때의 빈 정보
lines: Having converted the same pose, check what information remains at zero and half a turn when returning to axis and angle.

scenes.title: 정보가 부족하면 각도를 추측하지 않습니다
lines: The red body direction is visible, but that line alone does not determine the complete rotation axis.
This is the blue board direction in a different excerpt.
We will not guess information that is hidden.
The calculation uses the declared inputs and exceptional-case rules to verify the same orientation.

scenes.title: 변환한 숫자는 같은 방향을 만들까요
lines: Insert the midpoint of a ninety-degree rotation into the formulas, including their exceptional cases, and verify the same direction vector.

scenes.title: 끝 자세와 검산의 목적 연결하기
lines: Finally follow the body and board directions together through the action.
The red body line and blue board line represent different objects. Compare the input and output direction of the same object.
The worked numerical example fixed the camera and axes to verify that comparison.
We have not extracted the game internal rotation values. Next define moving points as lines and bounds.

scenes.title: 회전한 물체를 선과 경계로 다루는 다음 단계
lines: To use the position and orientation transformations just announced in game space, first define what moves and how far it reaches.
The next lesson builds lines and rays from points and tests ranges with spheres and boxes. We will then connect rotation and translation to changes in those shapes and bounds.
